name: Trisomy 18 (Edwards Syndrome)

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Cytogenetic Diagnostic Criteria for Trisomy 18

criteria.description: Presence of an extra full or partial chromosome 18 confirmed by karyotype or FISH
Micrognathia, prominent occiput, low-set malformed ears
Ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, patent ductus arteriosus
Characteristic hand posture with overlapping index finger over middle finger
Intrauterine growth restriction and postnatal failure to thrive

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Chromosomal confirmation of trisomy 18 plus presence of at least two major clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily confirmed by cytogenetic analysis; clinical features support suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Clenched fists with overlapping index finger
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic hand posture seen in majority of cases
searchTerms: tight fists with index finger over middle

pathognomonic.notes: Small lower jaw contributing to feeding difficulties

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., VSD, ASD, PDA)

searchTerms: baby smaller than expected in womb

common.notes: Due to poor suck and swallowing coordination

searchTerms: ears set low and abnormally shaped
unusually shaped ears placed low on head

occasional.notes: Abdominal wall defect with herniation of viscera
Defect in diaphragm causing lung compression
Spina bifida or encephalocele occasionally reported
searchTerms: spinal cord and brain tube defects

occasional.notes: Reduced muscle tone contributing to motor delays
Including horseshoe kidney or cystic dysplasia

searchTerms: split lip and/or roof of mouth

laboratory: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein in maternal serum screening
Abnormal prenatal screening markers (e.g., low PAPP-A)
imaging: Ultrasound showing intrauterine growth restriction and congenital anomalies
genetic: Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirming extra chromosome 18
other: Prenatal diagnosis via chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of midline facial defects such as cleft lip/palate
Lack of severe congenital malformations typical of trisomy 18

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects causing heart failure
Marked feeding difficulties with failure to thrive
references: Jones KL. Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation. 7th ed. 2013.
Botto LD, et al. Trisomy 18: clinical features and epidemiology. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2003.
